title: Singapore Police Force Recruitment 2026: SPF Guide
metaDescription: Singapore Police Force recruitment 2026: Direct-Entry Inspector and Sergeant schemes, starting salaries, sign-on bonuses and Academy training explained.
headline: Singapore Police Force Recruitment 2026: Schemes, Salaries and Training

sections.title: Entry schemes and requirements
sections.content:
The Singapore Police Force runs several entry schemes, and your qualification decides which one you can apply for. Direct-Entry Inspector requires a pass degree in any discipline, while Direct-Entry Sergeant is open to applicants whose academic qualifications are assessed by the force, and the Policing-Study Diploma Programme takes NITEC or Higher NITEC holders. All schemes require normal colour vision, and male applicants must hold a Physical Employment Standard (PES) grade of A or B1, while women are exempt from that standard.

Male applicants must also have completed full-time National Service, unless they are pre-enlistees, who discharge their service obligation by serving five years as regular officers on full salary. The force assesses academic qualifications and relevant work experience when setting starting pay, so two officers in the same scheme may start on different salaries.

sections.title: Pay, bonuses and benefits
sections.content:
The SPF publishes its starting salaries, which is unusual among police services. Direct-Entry Inspectors start at up to S$6,704 per month with a S$20,000 sign-on bonus, while Direct-Entry Sergeants start at up to S$3,860 per month with a S$35,000 sign-on bonus. Both bonuses are paid in two tranches, one on appointment and one on confirmation of service, rather than as a lump sum on day one, which matters when budgeting your first year.

Officers also receive retirement benefits under the INVEST scheme, with a contribution of 13.25 per cent of gross salary for Inspectors and 7.75 per cent for Sergeants credited monthly until age 57. A strategic payment scheme pays cash payouts of three months' salary at the 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, 15th, 20th and 25th years of service, and an annual Police (INVEST) payment of 0.75 to 1.5 months applies as officers advance.

sections.title: Training and career progression
sections.content:
Training is residential at the Home Team Academy, lasting nine months for Direct-Entry Inspectors, before posting into investigation, command and staff rotations. Officers progress through the Home Team rank structure, with opportunities in criminal investigation, community policing, traffic, intelligence and specialist units, and senior officers may move into command and policy roles.

The SPF is one of Singapore's largest uniformed services, and its officers work closely with other Home Team agencies on national security, major events and emergency response. Applicants should be prepared for shift work, weekend duties and public-facing responsibilities, and for the high standards of conduct expected of officers both on and off duty.

faqs.q: What qualifications do you need to join the Singapore Police Force?
faqs.a: Direct-Entry Inspector requires a pass degree in any discipline, while Direct-Entry Sergeant is open to applicants whose academic qualifications are assessed by the force. The Policing-Study Diploma Programme accepts NITEC or Higher NITEC holders. All applicants need normal colour vision, and male applicants must hold a PES grade of A or B1 and have completed full-time National Service.

faqs.q: How much does a Singapore police officer earn in 2026?
faqs.a: Direct-Entry Inspectors start at up to S$6,704 per month with a S$20,000 sign-on bonus, while Direct-Entry Sergeants start at up to S$3,860 per month with a S$35,000 sign-on bonus. Both bonuses are paid in two tranches, on appointment and on confirmation. Officers also receive INVEST retirement contributions and periodic strategic payments throughout their careers.

faqs.q: How long is Singapore police officer training?
faqs.a: Training is residential at the Home Team Academy, lasting nine months for Direct-Entry Inspectors, covering law, investigation, police procedures, physical training and leadership. After training, officers are posted into operational roles such as investigation, neighbourhood policing and command support, with further specialist courses available as their careers progress.

faqs.q: Do male and female applicants face different SPF requirements?
faqs.a: Yes, in one respect: male applicants must hold a Physical Employment Standard grade of A or B1 and have completed full-time National Service, while female applicants are exempt from the PES requirement. Normal colour vision is required for everyone, and academic and character standards apply equally. Pre-enlistee men discharge their National Service obligation by serving five years as regular officers.
